raw_case_text:
A 55-year-old previously healthy man presented with fever, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, myalgia, and dyspnea for three days after working in paddy fields. On admission, he was conscious, with low blood pressure (94/63 mmHg) and tachycardia (pulse rate 145 beats/min). There were bibasal lung crepitations, and urine output was only 10 mL over 4 hours. Admission blood tests indicated leucopenia and severe thrombocytopenia (Table 1).
After crystalloid fluid resuscitation noradrenaline was initiated to maintain blood pressure, intravenous ceftriaxone was commenced, and the patient was transferred to the medical intensive care unit (ICU). Due to severity of leptospirosis, intravenous methylprednisolone was administered for 3 days, and multiple platelet transfusions were given to correct thrombocytopenia. As oliguria persisted, intermittent hemodialysis was initiated. Dopamine was added due to persistent hypotension.
Chest radiograph indicated severe pulmonary hemorrhagic syndrome (Figure 1). Echocardiogram showed hypokinetic anterior wall motion and moderate mitral and tricuspid regurgitation. The patient was electively intubated and ventilated due to respiratory acidosis and hypoxia. Despite treatment, thrombocytopenia and abnormal liver function tests persisted (Table 1). Therapeutic plasma exchange was performed, and meropenem was commenced.
By Day 8, the patient was stable and afebrile, allowing for gradual withdrawal of inotropes. Leptospira microscopic agglutination test (MAT) became positive with a high titer. Blood picture showed low-grade hemolysis with a few red cell fragments.
On Day 21, the patient experienced fresh rectal bleeding. Upper gastroesophageal endoscopy revealed multiple gastric erosions, and colonoscopy revealed features of ischemic colitis. Blood and fresh frozen plasma were transfused, and intravenous proton pump inhibitor infusion was commenced. Exploratory laparotomy revealed extensive bowel necrosis from terminal ileum to the hepatic flexure with perforation and abscess formation of posterior wall of the ascending colon. Histopathology of affected areas confirmed these changes (Figure 2). There was no evidence of vasculitis in the rest of the peritoneal viscera. Standard right hemicolectomy and elective tracheostomy were performed.
On postoperative Day 1, the patient became unstable with hypotension and severe acidosis. Intact exteriorized bowel ends which had looked healthy at surgery showed features of ischemic necrosis. Since the patient's condition was unstable, further surgical exploration was abandoned. He succumbed on Day 27 of illness due to multiorgan failure.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 55-year-old male presenting with fever, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, myalgias, and dyspnea for 3 days following agricultural work in paddy fields.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Symptoms began 3 days prior to admission following work in paddy fields, presenting with fever, watery diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, generalized myalgias, and shortness of breath. On arrival, he was severely oliguric (10 mL urine over 4 hours) with shock and respiratory distress. He deteriorated into severe acute respiratory failure and refractory shock requiring intubation, inotropes, hemodialysis, and plasma exchange. On illness day 21, he developed acute fresh rectal bleeding, severe anemia, and peritonitis.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy. Epidemiological exposure: agricultural work in paddy fields prior to symptom onset.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports fever, nausea, vomiting, watery diarrhea, generalized myalgias, dyspnea, and rectal bleeding. Home medications: none. Allergies: not documented.

objective.physical_examination: On admission: conscious, hypotensive (blood pressure 94/63 mmHg) and tachycardic (pulse rate 145 beats/min). Respiratory: bibasal lung crepitations. Renal: profound oliguria (10 mL over 4 hours). On day 21: abdominal tenderness, peritoneal signs, and ischemic exteriorized bowel stoma.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count revealed leukopenia and severe thrombocytopenia; blood smear demonstrated low-grade microangiopathic hemolysis with red cell fragments. Liver function tests: persistently abnormal transaminases and hyperbilirubinemia. Renal function: severe oliguric acute kidney injury. Chest radiography: severe pulmonary hemorrhagic syndrome. Transthoracic echocardiogram: hypokinetic anterior wall motion with moderate mitral and tricuspid regurgitation.
objective.advanced_workup: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy: multiple gastric mucosal erosions. Colonoscopy: findings of ischemic colitis. Exploratory laparotomy: extensive transmural bowel necrosis extending from the terminal ileum to the hepatic flexure, with perforation and localized abscess formation along the posterior wall of the ascending colon. Histopathology confirmed transmural necrosis without evidence of systemic vasculitis in other peritoneal viscera.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Severe leptospirosis (Weil's disease) confirmed by Leptospira microscopic agglutination test (MAT) positive with a high diagnostic titer. Disease manifestations included severe pulmonary hemorrhage syndrome, septic and cardiogenic shock with acute myocardial dysfunction (anterior wall hypokinesis, MR/TR), anuric acute kidney injury requiring hemodialysis, microangiopathic hemolytic thrombocytopenia, and extensive ischemic bowel necrosis with ascending colon perforation and abscess formation.
Plan & Treatment: Crystalloid resuscitation, noradrenaline and dopamine inotropic support; antimicrobial therapy with IV ceftriaxone, escalated to meropenem; IV methylprednisolone for 3 days; intermittent hemodialysis; multiple platelet concentrates, fresh frozen plasma, and packed red blood cell transfusions; therapeutic plasma exchange; invasive mechanical ventilation; IV proton pump inhibitor infusion; emergency exploratory laparotomy with right hemicolectomy, abdominal drainage, and elective tracheostomy.
Outcome: On postoperative day 1, patient developed recurrent ischemic necrosis of exteriorized bowel ends with refractory acidosis and shock; surgical exploration was abandoned due to extreme instability, and he succumbed on Day 27 of illness due to multiorgan failure.
